Analog output from the optodes is produced by using a digital to analog converter (DAC). DAC configuration was initially only done at power up or reset, but firmware version 4.6.4 began updating configuration each time the analog output value was updated to ensure long-term continuous operation. Unfortunately, this also produced a voltage jump, creating erratic noise in the output data. The firmware has been corrected, but only the onboard-calculated Stern-Volmer values [DO from Onboard Calculation (L1 product; 'ctd_tc_oxygen') and DO from Onboard Calculation - Corrected (L2 product; 'dissolved_oxygen')] should be used during this annotated time range, NOT the 'DO from Phase' data which contain the noisy analog signal.

On 17 August 2020, at ~1824 hours PDT, the south cable line went offline due to an over-current event. Submarine cable repair operations commenced August 2021 utilizing an industry cable repair/installation ship, with support from the R/V Thompson and ROV Jason. The faulty Primary Node PN1B was recovered, removed from the system, and jointing activities of the replacement PN1B were completed on 15 August. The final bight was successfully deployed to the seafloor on 23 August 2021. The RCA south cable line has been powered and PN1A, PN1C, and PN1D are now fully operational.

The Oregon Offshore profiler pod was mid-profile and 31m below the surface when a power shutdown occurred following a short circuit in the south cable line on 17 August. This created a potential hazard, so on 21 August 2020 at ~1700 PDT the cable was parted by the Jason ROV and the pod was recovered by the Thompson. The profiler platform remained operational, but no data were available from the shallow profiler instruments until the pod was replaced during the summer 2021 maintenance cruise.

Adverse weather in Pacific City, OR on 13 Jan 2021 resulted in multiple loss of power events at the cable shore station. This resulted in a fault in the emergency diesel control system and loss of power to the Cabled Array. NMS server issues were resolved and power began to be restored on 15 Jan.

The SC01B Profiler stopped at the top of its cast on May 3rd, due to an excessive levelwind drive current. The profiler pod was suspended near the surface until May 7th. The pod was left in that position until May 16 when an attempt to extend cable was successful, and the pod moved from 185 m to 178 m. However, it is still likely that the winch cable is badly mis-wrapped. The nodes are powered and all instruments are sampling, but the pod is stationary. Further profiling operations are under consideration.

Instrument is sampling irregularly and at a reduced rate, although the raw data show timestamps for the expected sampling frequency, and currently appears to be responding normally to manual commands. A ground fault was noted and port current is abnormally high following a power cycle. High current seems correlated to opening and closing the serial port (current low when serial port closed). Downloaded/erased instrument, tried running blank sample and cycling pump. No major issues noted other than the continued high current while serial port opened. Power cycled instrument, then re-launched and switched digi back to TCP mode. Data became inconsistent and then invalid. Instrument has a large ground fault (202,3), was powered down and alarms silenced.

Digi timestamps were not enabled, which is likely why data were not appearing in the proper places. They have now been enabled. Instrument was responsive and Mission Execution appears to be running normally, though there were some interruptions in mission execution earlier in this period.

In an effort to reduce noise in the CW data, we ran in passive FM mode using EK80 diagnostic tools, and found some large spikes at the target frequencies. We then narrowed the FM settings to frequency ranges that avoid the largest noise spikes and set up an advanced sequence with sequential pinging at one ping per second (3 seconds to cycle through all 3 transducers). The following frequency ranges were used: 200: 192-197 khz; 120: 125-128 khz; 38: 42-44 khz. Following this test, the system was returned to CW mode.

EK-80 control software updated to version 24.6 and started advanced sequence to run interleaved CW-complex and FM mode pings. Initial alternating ping set-up is simultaneous 38CW+200CW, simultaneous 38FM+200FM, then 120 CW, and then 120 FM. Ping interval for all ping groups = 500 ms (4 s for full alternating ping cycle), pulse duration for all FM pings = 8.192 ms, max power for all pings (38 - 450 W, 120/200 - 150 W), full frequency ranges for all FM pings (35-45, 90-170, 160-260 kHz), range set to 220 m (same as previous).

Ping Interval: 1000 ms, max power and 1.024 ms ping lengths for all frequencies.

A memory leak in SC01B's winch control GUI caused a winch trip that stopped profiling at a depth of ~7 m. The profiler pod was docked, encoders were reset, and the pod was returned to the parking position in standard sampling mode ready for the next profile.

SF01B was at 7 m and turning around to begin descent when the winch controller experienced an overcurrent and tripped. Pod was restarted and retracted to 180 m for troubleshooting. The profiler was then retracted and docked, minimum depth for top-of-profile turn-around was changed from 5 meters to 15 meters to mitigate overcurrent incidents, and profiling resumed on 16 October.

Instrument port experienced an A/D i2c error and the channel self-disabled. Re-enabling repeatedly resulted in the same error, so the DC/DC converter for that port may have failed. Instrument offline.

The minimum depth for top-of-profile turn-around was changed from 15 meters to 10 meters after mitigation of over-current trips occurring at the top of the profile, to try to measure important features in the upper water column without triggering winch overcurrent alarms.

Shallow profilers were parked and sampling was paused as a precaution while a DAS experiment was connected to the system. They were returned to standard sampling mode once the connection was complete.
